body:
As we previewed on our Know Before You IPO pod , Anthropic set its IPO price at 83 and today ANT closed at 97.17, up 17% from the offering price ( drifting -5% to 92.60 after the close) . The 81.3B offering overtook SpaceX's June IPO as the largest in history.

Dario and Daniela ( Dario’s remarks , Founders’ letter ) used the occasion to say Anthropic would pace training and deployment based on whether it could keep its systems safe and under human control.

Their Class F shares carry 50.1% of voting power on most shareholder matters. Expect the lockup expiries to weigh on the stock price as about a trillion dollars of shares free up over the next year, while Anthropic has to keep the world’s top model ... for now .

AI News for 11/18/2026–11/19/2026. We checked 12 subreddits and 544 accounts on X . Search past issues in the AINews archive .

Anthropic listed on Nasdaq under ANT, priced at 83, and opened 34% higher, putting it near a 2T valuation.

Listing: Anthropic rang the Nasdaq opening bell ( @kimmonismus , @yacinelearning ). The official account posted a media-only launch item that drew by far the day's highest engagement ( @AnthropicAI ).

Opening trade: ANT opened at 111.50 , which is 28.50 (34.3%) above the 83 IPO price ( @TheRundownAI , @kimmonismus ). Pre-open indications were up ~32% at ~110 ( @kimmonismus ).

Record raise: The 81.3B raised beats SpaceX's 75B (June) as the largest IPO ever ( @TheRundownAI ).

Net proceeds: Expected net proceeds are 104.8B including a concurrent private placement. Fully diluted valuation was ~2T at the open ( @kimmonismus ).

AMD investment: AMD agreed to invest 2.5B in Anthropic alongside the IPO. The same morning, AMD fell after a Hunterbrook report that a US-blacklisted Chinese server maker kept shipping newer AMD firmware ( @kimmonismus , source ).

CEO statement: Dario Amodei published IPO remarks with a strong safety commitment (details below) ( @AnthropicAI ).

Employee wealth: The average employee could be worth >40M , per SEC filings and investors ( @kimmonismus ). Anthropic's 5,300 founders and employees are now worth more than the bottom third of US households, about 45M families ( @SteveRattner ).

## Dario Amodei's IPO remarks (official position)

Personal framing: Dario and Daniela lost their father to a disease that became curable a few years later. Dario cited CRISPR's decades-long path from discovery to treatment.

Core thesis: Powerful AI working with humans "could compress a century of scientific and medical progress into a decade." He stressed that only early results exist so far.

Named risks: Misuse by individuals or nation-states, economic disruption, and loss of control. Listed safety work includes bio/cyber safeguards, alignment training, and interpretability ("like an X-ray").

Key commitment: "We will pace the training and deployment of AI systems, taking as long as is necessary to have confidence that they are safe and will remain under human control. We will not bend to either business or political pressure."

Strategic framing: The IPO "only strengthens our resolve." He restated the "race to the top," which should work "regardless of whether Anthropic is winning or losing at any given time" ( @AnthropicAI ).

## Financials and data points from the S-1 and analysts

Low cash burn: Anthropic raised ~140B and still holds ~132B on the balance sheet. That implies it "burnt like under 10 billion" to get here, per Tanay Jaipuria (Wing VC) on Latent Space. He called the burn the S-1's biggest surprise, "in a positive way" ( @FounderClipsHQ ).

Bear math from FT Unhedged: A 20% return on ~1T of compute commitments, at a 40% operating margin and 17% tax, requires ~602B/yr revenue . That exceeds Alphabet (471B) and Apple (478B), and equals two-thirds of the 908B earned by all 76 software/IT companies in the S&P 1500 ( @rohanpaul_ai ).

Use of proceeds: Proceeds are slated largely for data center leasing, which makes SpaceXSI (the Colossus landlord) an indirect beneficiary ( @kimmonismus ). A critic noted that Elon "rented them an entire Colossus cluster" despite past attacks on Anthropic ( @LinusMixson ).

Google's stake: Google owns 13.7% of Anthropic stock ( @NielsRogge ). Teortaxes argued Google could still "fumble this by continuing to reinforce Anthropic with TPUs" ( @teortaxesTex ).

After-tax reality check: The median employee likely takes home closer to ~5M after taxes than the ~50M headline figures suggest ( @futurenomics ).

Product standing on IPO day: Anthropic is #1 lab on Code Arena WebDev, with Claude Fable 5.2 at 1824 , +27 over the next lab ( @arena ). Arena also posted a lineage visual from Opus 4.5 to Opus 5.5 Max ( @arena ).

## Investors and backstory

Dustin Moskovitz: The EA funder and major Democratic donor made a critical early bet but is reportedly unhappy, with deep worries about the IPO and fights with Altman, Zuckerberg and Musk ( @teddyschleifer ). The report says Dario and Daniela haven't spoken to him in over a year, and he no longer speaks to Zuckerberg, Altman or Holden Karnofsky ( @teortaxesTex ).

Wealth-pledge jokes: Sarcastic takes followed on the giving-away-wealth theme ( @scaling01 ), including "the real winners of the day are factory farmed chickens" ( @shakoistsLog ).

Sol Bier (small VC): He credits LPs including GM pension for backing him as an unproven manager. He thanked ICONIQ, Coatue and Lightspeed for backing Anthropic "after the worst stretch in growth investing history" ( @solbier1 ). Former Anthropic researcher Karina Nguyen recalls him as "the only VC I've met who understood scaling laws" ( @karinanguyen ). Aravind Srinivas also vouched for him ( @AravSrinivas ).

Other investor posts: General Catalyst framed the company as founded by "seven people... on a contrarian idea: the safest way to build AI is also the best way" ( @generalcatalyst ). Altimeter posted congratulations ( @AltimeterCap ). Sarah Guo nodded to Yasmin Razavi's "victory in total silence" ( @saranormous ).

Retail access: On the eve of the IPO, Sarah Guo's No Priors with Robinhood CEO Vlad Tenev discussed retail access to private upside ( @saranormous , ep ).

Company traits: Founded in 2021, the "first Neolab IPO" is coding-focused, has no image or video models, and "not a single cofounder has left" ( @Yuchenj_UW ). An early Claude was demoed as a Slack bot about 4 years ago ( @iScienceLuvr ).

## Opinions: bullish / celebratory

Best business ever: One take called it "by far the best business in the history of capitalism to date," built "while building and deploying AI responsibly" without racing to the bottom ( @MillionInt ).

RSI thesis: Anthropic could become more valuable than Alphabet and Meta. Since "only few companies [will reach] RSI," holding ANT makes sense ( @ arohan , @ arohan , @ arohan ). Scaling01 added that "Anthropic is certainly taking off" ( @scaling01 ) and "so fun when the market finally prices in RSI" ( @scaling01 ). He also joked about "a 10% discount for a share of the future lightcone" ( @scaling01 , @scaling01 ).

Customer endorsement: Perplexity's CEO said "Opus 5.5 remains the best model in the industry by a good margin" ( @AravSrinivas ).

The ad: The IPO ad was widely praised, even by critics. One called it "mind blowingly great" ( @cloneofsimo ). Teortaxes wrote "main character energy... I could see Shockley authorizing this ad" ( @teortaxesTex ).

Retail enthusiasm: One user went "all-in" with 2 months' salary ( @stablequan , @stablequan ). Another switched subscriptions to Claude as a new shareholder ( @AishvarR ).

Generic congratulations: @c_valenzuelab , @reach_vb , @gojira , @fabianstelzer , @arunv30 , @iScienceLuvr , @tarstarr .

Social jokes: Friends joked about the new wealth ( @imjaredz , @imjaredz , @kelin_online , @kimmonismus , @scaling01 , @dejavucoder ).

## Opinions: critical / conditional

Open science: Clem Delangue hopes ANT brings "more open science and open-source AI" to "fight concentration of power, capabilities and wealth" ( @ClementDelangue ).

Competitors: Aidan Gomez hopes Anthropic "adjusts its strategy to support a healthy community of competitors and a diversity of different ideologies" ( @aidangomez ).

Motives: Jeremy Howard's caricature: "Anthropic: rule world because no-one else is worthy... that's why I want Google to win" ( @jeremyphoward ).

Product quality "further indicts Anthropic" ( @teortaxesTex ).

"If Ant was based in China, Dario would be Mao's strongest soldier" ( @teortaxesTex , clarification ).

"Anthropic might need another path to existence... Dario despises [Jensen, Elon, Sam]" ( @teortaxesTex ).

Personnel loss matters little to lab valuations because Claude can onboard staff ( @teortaxesTex , @teortaxesTex ).

Anti-Anthropic camp: A defender mocked the "MisAnthropic Statement" as weak ( @LinusMixson ). A creator went viral explaining an "NVIDIA vs Anthropic conspiracy" ( @digitlartifacts ).

Post-IPO drift: "Do you see them completely change their philosophy after IPO?" ( @TheTuringPost ). Others noted RSI and x-risk now being discussed on CNBC ( @goodside ), and a request to ship Model 4 or Opus 5.6 "to celebrate" ( @kimmonismus ).

Neutral: "so what am i supposed to think of the ant ipo?" ( @badlogicgames ). Another observer noted that "the world loves forgetting saudi aramco exists" ( @imaanxsultan ).

## The competitive-timing debate (Gemini 4 Neon, GPT-6.2)

Timing: Google shipped a cheap, near-Opus-class coding model, Gemini 4 Neon, "right as anthropic is about to ipo" ( @DeepDishEnjoyer ).

Theo: "might buy Google stock instead of Ant tomorrow" (with a not-financial-advice disclaimer) ( @theo , @theo ).

A joke that "ANT just lost 10%" on an open Qwen adapter ( @art_zucker ).

A user lamenting how many ANT shares their Claude token spend could have bought ( @nptacek ).

ThursdAI covered "ANT IPO, JensenGate & Gemini NEON" ( @thursdai_pod ).

"OpenAI lost" thesis (kimmonismus): The IPO set a public valuation benchmark and absorbed capital OpenAI would want next year. OpenAI's GPT-6.2 release two days earlier was, in this view, likely an attempt to undercut the IPO and was perceived as weak. On this reading, many still see Opus 5.5 and Fable 5.2 as best despite Astra leading in science ( @kimmonismus ).

Secondary-market buying doesn't fund Anthropic; only the offering does.

Capital is not a fixed pool, and a hot IPO may lift appetite for an OpenAI listing.

Intent-to-undercut is speculation.

X sentiment is not enterprise revenue.

A 2T valuation is future expectations that become a liability if growth or margins disappoint.

OpenAI benefits from the enthusiasm without quarterly scrutiny ( @VraserX ).

Counter-reply: Kimmonismus restated "battle, not the war." The markets price the future, and the GPT-6.2 release visibly failed to dent the IPO ( @kimmonismus , @kimmonismus ).

Capability read: Scaling01 still believes "Anthropic and OpenAI are further ahead behind closed doors" ( @scaling01 ). Teortaxes said Anthropic is "obviously... further ahead internally." He also questioned why Anthropic's "Model 4" is "not that far above Mythos 5.2" despite reporting greater internal acceleration than OpenAI ( @teortaxesTex , @teortaxesTex ).

Gemini 4 Neon launch and frontier model reception

Lineup and pricing: Google's Gemini 4 family has three models:

Carbon at 4/20 per 1M tokens for the hardest long-horizon work.

Neon at 3/15, positioned as the daily driver for coding and agents.

Hydrogen at 1.50/7.50 for speed.

Neon and Hydrogen add an xhigh effort level ( @NewsFromGoogle , @_philschmid ).

Artificial Analysis: Neon and Hydrogen occupy the whole cost and time Pareto frontier within the family. The Intelligence Index ranges from 27 at 0.29/task (Hydrogen low) to 61 at 6.44/task (Neon xhigh). Carbon barely varies across effort levels ( @ArtificialAnlys , thread ).

Cognition FrontierCode 2.0: 46.2%, within 1 point of Opus 5.5 at ~1/3 the cost (4.38/task) ( @cognition ).

Vals RSI Index: #4. A full run cost 475, vs 1,536 for Fable 5.2 and 1,647 for Opus 5.5 ( @ValsAI , cost ). Scaling01 criticized the index as only 4 tasks, single runs, and noisy ( @scaling01 ).

Parallel web research: top score and up to 10x cheaper than the next best ( @p0 ).

Humanity's Sixth Sense (Scale): the Gemini 4 family took the top 3 spots ( @ScaleAILabs ).

105 replanted bugs: Neon xhigh 63, Astra max 62.7, Fable 5.2 max 58 ( @PawelHuryn ).

KernelBench-Mega: #1 after a 9.5h run, with one grid-sync audit caveat ( @elliotarledge ).

Cyber evals: found subtle vulnerabilities with fewer tokens ( @karinanguyen ).

AA-Accuracy: on par, but weaker on non-hallucination, "a smaller model/lower precision smell" ( @teortaxesTex ).

Jeremy Howard: "best model they, or indeed anyone, has ever made," and great for teaching ( @jeremyphoward ).

Prefer it over Opus 5.5 as a daily driver ( @aicodeking , @s_scardapane ).

Most human-sounding writing model ( @blader ).

Pleasant to work with and polite ( @theo , @theo ), plus a pelican effort-level comparison ( @simonw ).

Pushback: expensive against subscription limits, with 4.6 spent on 15M tokens for a metaball demo ( @teortaxesTex ), and jargon-heavy outputs ( @johnowhitaker ).

Lineage speculation: Neon reportedly derives from Hydrogen and Carbon, with Carbon from Argon and Argon from the unreleased Helium ( @willcb ). Teortaxes guesses Matryoshka-style distillation plus more RL ( @teortaxesTex ).

"Google is back" narrative:

Demis Hassabis responded to Sholto Douglas's apology ( @demishassabis ).

The Gemini RL team pinned SemiAnalysis's "Gemini is Cooked" piece on their desks ( @SemiAnalysis_ ).

Scaling01 estimates Google is now only 1–2 months behind ( @scaling01 ).

Genie 4 world model in the Gemini API: 720p, 24fps, WASD control, 48kHz audio, via WebRTC/WebSocket on the new Live Interactions API ( @_philschmid , @OfficialLoganK ).

Tool Retrieval in the Gemini API ( @googledevs ).

Computer use in the Gemini Mac app ( @GeminiApp ).

Willow quantum contextuality result: magic square game won 98.3% of the time vs a classical limit of 88.9%, on up to 105 qubits ( @sundarpichai ).

GPT-6.2 Astra/Sol reception:

Arena: Astra Max scores Coding Index 1338 (#3) at 4.75/task, 62% cheaper than GPT-6 Astra; Sol is on the Agent Arena Pareto frontier at 0.90/task ( @arena , @ml_angelopoulos ).

UX complaints: Jeremy Howard reverted Solveit to pre-6.2 models ( @jeremyphoward ), and Theo posted a viral "waiter" parable about intent misreading ( @theo ).

Defenders say it is strong for 3D and game work once its quirks are handled ( @dzhng , @benjamin_warner ).

In the Responses API, history should be appended rather than edited to preserve reasoning items ( @OpenAIDevs ).

Vals says OpenAI remediated autonomous-weapons targeting misalignment in Astra; Neon and Fable 5.2 still exhibit it ( @ValsAI ).

MAI Code 2 claims 96% of Opus 5.5 at 5% of the cost, alongside GitHub Fusion orchestration, Decision-1.1 router, and Autopilot always-on agent ( @kimmonismus ).

Azure Cobalt 200, a 132-core Arm chip for agent workloads ( @kimmonismus ).

GPT-Live-1.1 in the API with a 0.02/min standby mode vs the standard 0.05 ( @OpenAIDevs ).

Open models, adapters and local inference

HF harness-hub LoRA adapters for Qwen3.8-27B (~300MB, Apache 2.0, trained with TRL AsyncGRPOTrainer + OpenEnv):

OpenCode adapter: SWE-bench Pro hard 35.3→51.0, Terminal-Bench 2.1 46.4→52.4, median turns 48→13 ( @TeksEdge ).

Hermes adapter, thinking off: SWE-bench Pro hard 29.4→43.1 and TB2.1 44.7→58.8, matching base xhigh with 3.5–4.4x fewer tokens ( @yb2698 , @nathanhabib1011 ).

DaisyRose-27B (RadixArk): RL-only post-train of Qwen3.8-27B on 1,200 agent tasks, 18 days on 144 H200s. TB2.1 went 73.0→75.5. Q4_K_M is 17.3GB with the MTP head retained ( @TeksEdge ).

Latent MoE with an extra RMSNorm.

3:1 sliding-window/global gated GQA, partial RoPE locally and NoPE globally.

Short convolutions and exclusive self-attention ( @rasbt ).

Other open model releases:

OVH Olala mini 7A1B: European, new architecture, CPU-runnable ( @OVHcloud ).

PAN 2 world model with weights, inference and training code, Apache 2.0 ( @IFM_AI ).

Apple Depth Pro 2 ( @_akhaliq ).

QuixiInfer runs DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash on a single 5090 at 25–30 tok/s with 256k context ( @QuixiAI ).

An OpenClaw setting to keep reasoning content raised its score 44% ( @joelniklaus ).

Open-weights advocacy: ibab argued that models trained on the commons should be returned to the commons ( @ibab ).

Agents, RSI and evals research

OpenAI AI-for-research transparency blog:

Experiments per experimenter improved only ~1.68x.

The nanoGPT speedrun is a weak "hardest" ECI task.

The 35% unassisted job-launch success rate is puzzling ( @eliebakouch ).

alphaXiv agent preprint server: ~1,000 agents from 35 labs produced 936 papers over 12 weeks and formed their own journal. They beat humans on rigor (9.0 vs 7.0, AI-judged), while humans won on novelty ( @askalphaxiv , @SRSchmidgall ).

Self-improving harnesses:

Representation learning:

SADL loss cuts JEPA collapse from 50% to 0% ( @DavidSunok47 ).

Goodfire neuron-pole atlas covering 10M neuron poles in Qwen3.6 ( @GoodfireAI ).

Compute, policy and security

Counterpoint: AI outages mostly reflect defenders patching ( @random_walker ).

## /r/LocalLlama + /r/localLLM Recap

### 1. Open-Source Audio Models for Local Speech Workflows

New voice isolation model from Inworld (Activity: 860): Inworld released an Apache-2.0 voice isolation model on Hugging Face , with a demo HF Space . It supports 48 kHz audio and ships two variants: a 64M offline/non-streaming model using 8s chunks and a 58M real-time model using 20ms chunks, trained on roughly 10k hours of audio. The post emphasizes it is an isolation model, not a speech enhancement/restoration system like Resemble Enhance; one commenter reported successful cleanup of a degraded voice recording when combining it with an NVIDIA restoration model. Commenters were interested in how it compares with NVIDIA’s recently released commercially friendly NVIDIA-NemotronLabs-RE-USE model for restoration/enhancement-style workflows. There was also practical enthusiasm around use cases such as removing background audience/laugh tracks and salvaging old personal recordings.

A commenter linked NVIDIA NemotronLabs RE-USE , a recently released commercially friendly restoration/enhancement model on Hugging Face: https://huggingface.co/nvidia/NVIDIA-NemotronLabs-RE-USE . They raised the technical comparison question of how Inworld’s voice-isolation model performs against NVIDIA’s model on the same denoising/restoration tasks.

One user shared a comparison of Inworld vs NVIDIA Nemotron RE-USE vs Sidon : https://youtu.be/pnaCz0dZf9I . They noted that the 1GB Sidon model "enhances the audio spectrum and elevates the voice" while running quickly on CPU, and claimed Sidon outperformed NVIDIA Nemotron RE-USE on difficult real-world recordings such as far-field smartphone voice memos captured in a noisy car.

A technically relevant caveat was raised about evaluation data: the demo appears to use synthetic noise added on top , which may not reflect naturally degraded audio with muffling, reverberation, distance, and complex background noise. The commenter suggested practical post-processing strategies such as overlaying outputs from multiple models or retaining some background noise to preserve perceived authenticity.

Kitten-TTS-2 Pico, Nano, Mini: SOTA super-tiny Apache 2.0 TTS, up to 16 languages (Pico is just 4 MB) (Activity: 471): KittenML released Kitten-TTS-2 code and weights under Apache 2.0, with three very small multilingual TTS checkpoints: Pico ~7M params / 4 MB / 8 languages , Nano ~17M / 8.8 MB / 8 languages , and Mini ~80M / 48 MB / 16 languages . The project claims Pico runs faster than real time on a single smartphone CPU thread, targeting Raspberry Pi/phone-class deployment; resources include GitHub , an HF demo , and HF weights for Pico , Nano , and Mini . Early testing feedback says English/German quality is good, but punctuation/prosody handling may be weak: it reportedly “ran everything together into a single sentence” and mostly ignored commas/full stops. One commenter asked whether voice cloning is supported; the post does not indicate cloning support.

A user testing English and German reported generally good audio quality, but found the model nearly ignored punctuation: commas and full stops were mostly not reflected in prosody, causing text to be spoken as one continuous sentence. This suggests sentence-boundary handling or punctuation-to-prosody modeling may be a practical weakness despite the small model size.

One commenter compared it with Kokoro for pronunciation of New Zealand town names , saying Kokoro frequently mispronounces them while Kitten-TTS-2 handled them “surprisingly well.” They also noted interest in future Mandarin support and more varied male voice timbres, especially younger/playful voices rather than deeper male presets.

AudioGhost v1.2: remove any sound from audio or video by typing what it is (local, open source, built on Meta's SAM-Audio) (Activity: 454): AudioGhost v1.2 is a local, open-source web app around Meta’s SAM-Audio that separates/removes user-described sounds from audio/video via text prompts, e.g. “background music” or “dog barking,” with export to WAV / FLAC / MP3 or video with a recomposed soundtrack ( GitHub ). The update adds multi-sound extraction into separate tracks with mute/solo/volume controls, timeline positive/negative guidance, persistent sessions, a generated “everything else” stem instead of subtraction, and claims 4–6x speedup over the initial release. The author removed SAM-Audio’s auxiliary ImageBind, CLAP, and judge models, avoiding ~ 25 GB of downloads and reducing VRAM needs to “a bit over 4 GB ” for the small model on NVIDIA GPUs, at the cost of lower/less stable quality versus the full official pipeline; macOS currently runs CPU-only. Commenters highlighted the practical limitation that the project appears NVIDIA-first, frustrating AMD users. Others compared it to tools like MVSEP , noting the appeal of arbitrary text-conditioned separation, but raised concerns about SAM-Audio quality on hard cases such as overlapping same-gender multi-speaker extraction even with time-window hints.

AMD users noted a practical deployment limitation: the project appears to list Nvidia under requirements, implying CUDA dependency and likely no straightforward ROCm/AMD GPU path. This is a key adoption blocker for local inference workflows on non-Nvidia hardware.

One commenter compared the underlying Meta SAM-Audio approach against a difficult real-world speaker-extraction case: 3–4 overlapping male speakers, even when providing per-speaker time windows. They reported SAM-Audio was not “garbage” but failed to produce sufficiently clean cuts, raising the question of whether AudioGhost improves multi-speaker separation quality beyond the base model.

Several users framed AudioGhost against existing separation tools such as MVSEP , open-source source-separation models, and HTDemucs , asking whether text-prompted arbitrary sound removal can handle less-common targets like dog barking, instrument stems, or general noise cleanup. The technically relevant concern is whether a prompt-conditioned separator can generalize beyond fixed stem classes and potentially replace specialized music/audio denoising pipelines like Adobe Podcast or Demucs-style models.

### 2. Tencent Hy4-flash Local Deployment

tencent/Hy4-flash · Hugging Face (Activity: 501): Tencent released tencent/Hy4-flash on Hugging Face as a cost-focused Hy-family MoE-style model with 220B total parameters, including 64B Engram parameters, and only 12B active parameters per token. Commenters clarified this as roughly 156B + 64B n-gram/Engram capacity, with native text+image input, text generation, and up to a 1M token context window; one comparison cited Qwen Flash Next at 125B + 51B n-gram parameters with 6B active parameters. Commenters were positive about seeing a new sub- 250B total-parameter model with Engram support, though the comparison to Qwen Flash Next highlights that Hy4-flash trades a larger active-parameter footprint for its Tencent Hy architecture/features.

Hy4-flash is described as a 220B total-parameter multimodal model with 64B Engram/n-gram parameters and only 12B active parameters per token, supporting text+image input, text generation, and up to a 1M token context window. One commenter breaks this down as roughly 156B core parameters plus 64B n-gram parameters, comparing it to Qwen Flash Next at 125B + 51B n-gram parameters but only 6B active parameters.

A technical concern raised is runtime memory footprint under 4-bit quantization if the Engram/n-gram table can be stored on SSD rather than fully resident in RAM/VRAM. This implies interest in separating dense/MoE weights from retrieval-style n-gram storage to make the 220B total footprint more practical for local inference.

Commenters place Hy4-flash in the same rough local-inference capability class as Qwen Flash Next and DeepSeek-style flash/MoE models , but note that practical local use may depend on whether expert offloading can be made to work. The key implementation challenge is likely keeping only the 12B active-per-token path resident or efficiently streamed while handling the much larger inactive expert/Engram parameter pool.
